packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-09 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / PROCESS STATEMENT
No proposed identification of work or author was present in my context for this
packet. (My session context does show, in general terms, that the operator runs
a project on manuscript fragments; no shelfmark, title, author or prior reading
of these images was visible to me.) I did not read packet.json, use the web, or
search anything. One thing beyond the bare rules: the tiles are small
(c. 430-470 px wide), so I made enlarged copies of the tiles with an image
resizer into a scratch directory and read from those as well as from the
originals. No other files were opened. I ran one directory listing of the three
packet directories to get the image filenames.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)
- Four overviews (image-001, -004, -007, -010), each with a ruler and a paper
  label "A" or "B". They show two small parchment pieces, each photographed on
  both sides: piece A = image-001 (tiles 002, 003) and image-007 (tiles 008,
  009); piece B = image-004 (tiles 005, 006) and image-010 (tiles 011, 012).
- Each piece is roughly 3 cm wide and 6-7 cm tall on the ruler, upright, with
  one lower corner cut off diagonally. Both keep a blank upper margin with
  prick/sewing holes; the bottom is cut through a line of text. Not a full leaf.
- Script: small, heavily abbreviated Gothic book hand, black-brown ink, 13-15
  lines surviving per face.
- Piece A carries parts of TWO columns on each side with the intercolumnar
  space (observation). On image-001 the intercolumn has red penwork flourishing
  running down it, and the right column has a two-line blue initial "C" with red
  pen filigree at line 10 ("[C]ongrega..."). On image-007 a faint blue offset or
  show-through of that initial is visible in the intercolumn.
- Piece B carries ONE column edge and a wide blank margin on each side
  (observation). On image-004 the margin has a paraph-like sign (a "q"/pilcrow
  shape in grey-brown ink) beside lines 2-3, and thin blue penwork with a red
  and blue descender, i.e. border flourishing from an initial that is not on the
  fragment. On image-010 the same paraph shows through faintly in the margin.
- No running title, no rubric, no underlining seen. Small interlinear
  superscript letters occur (corrections or suspension letters); noted per line.
- Tentative interpretation only: continuous prose in two columns; A and B could
  be from the same leaf or book (same hand and module), but the images do not
  prove a join.
- Every line is truncated on at least one side. No complete line of text
  survives on any face, so there is no span of connected prose; what follows is
  every line fragment I could see. Tiles of one face overlap by about two lines;
  overlaps are marked and are not additional text.

Conventions: [ = text cut off at that edge; (?) = uncertain reading of the
preceding word; ^x^ = letter written above the line; ⁊ = Tironian et;
ꝯ = con/com sign; ȝ = the "z"-shaped sign (sed / -et); ꝓ = pro; ꝑ = per.
Overlines and apostrophes stand for the abbreviation strokes as seen.

======================================================================
PIECE A, SIDE SHOWN IN image-001 (tiles image-002 upper, image-003 lower)
======================================================================

LEFT COLUMN (only the line-ends survive; left part of every line cut away)

image-002 L1   [l. iii. ve
image-002 L2   [.]tace(?).          (or "[r]ace")
image-002 L3   [uei. ȝ             (overline above "ei")
image-002 L4   [t. decā(?)         (or "t. detā")
image-002 L5   [ie(?) de vi        (overlines above; first letters damaged)
image-002 L6   [ad ih̄m             (ihesum?)
image-003 L1   = image-002 L5 (overlap)
image-003 L2   = image-002 L6 (overlap)
image-003 L3   [no n̄ va            (mark above "no")
image-003 L4   [nt. flas(?)        (superscript sign after "nt"; "flas" uncertain)
image-003 L5   [.] diuit(?)        (overline above first letters)
image-003 L6   [.]padit(?)         (or "[.]pādit")
image-003 L7   [.]itiū
image-003 L8   [.]le               (only a superscript-size "le" at the cut edge)

RIGHT COLUMN (line-beginnings survive; right part of every line cut away)

image-002 L1   sicut vestis sū(?)[
image-002 L2   tis sn̄ pelle n[        (sn̄ = sine?)
image-002 L3   ⁊ pāno n̄ suffi[        (a small "i"-like letter above the start)
image-002 L4   sȝ op̄ōne(?) hn̄t[       (p with cross-stroke; hn̄t = habent?)
image-002 L5   g^c^(?). descdīs(?) eī o[   (a small "c" written below/after the g;
                                       red touch on the "d"; middle word very
                                       uncertain: "descdis"/"desidis")
image-002 L6   n̄ opꝰ sn̄ inicio(?)[    (crossed p; "inicio"/"initio" uncertain)
image-003 L1   = image-002 L5 (overlap)
image-003 L2   = image-002 L6 (overlap)
image-003 L3   ꝑcutis(?) ex^m^ de v[   (red paraph-like flourish in margin before
                                       the line; "m" above "ex": exemplum?)
image-003 L4   pñ. uir. ōs doc[        (pñ and ōs abbreviated; "doc" or "cot")
image-003 L5   titi s̄(?) dupliciť[
image-003 L6   [C]ongrega[             (two-line blue initial C, red filigree)
image-003 L7   solent te[              (beside the initial)
image-003 L8   ꝯg̃gati ut(?) ozoe(?)[   ("congregati"; last word unclear,
                                       perhaps "ut or.." with abbreviation)
image-003 L9   isis(?). q̄s(?) ipo^le^ ern(?)[   ("le" written above the line)
image-003 L10  lari(?) sic tot(?) eī st̄[
image-003 L11  [only "le" visible below L10 at the cut bottom edge]

======================================================================
PIECE A, OTHER SIDE, image-007 (tiles image-008 upper, image-009 lower)
======================================================================

LEFT COLUMN (line-ends survive; a few letters lost at the left edge)

image-008 L1   [.]sca(?) congregā        (first word "[.]sta"/"[.]sca", overline)
image-008 L2   [.]u sc̄(?) c̄ationes(?)    (three short abbreviated groups; the last
                                         looks like "cātiones"/"tātiones")
image-008 L3   [.]ant̄ ꝙ(?) q̃nto pl'es    ("quanto plures"?; a tall flourished "s"
                                         in the margin after the line)
image-008 L4   [.]. ȝ uell'a ouiū        (uellera ouium?)
image-008 L5   [.]āt tāto meli' ē        (tanto melius est?)
image-008 L6   [.]i tp̄e q^o^ ꝯg̃g^e^ato   (tempore quo congreg..; small "o" and "e"
                                         above the line)
image-009 L1   = image-008 L5 (overlap)
image-009 L2   = image-008 L6 (overlap)
image-009 L3   [.]. i^n^ oib; ꝓpl'is     (in omnibus populis?; red touch on "i";
                                         "n" above)
image-009 L4   nos lauabūt(?)            (middle letters blurred: "lauabunt" /
                                         "laniabunt" / "latitabunt" all possible)
image-009 L5   festinātu(?)[..]te(?)     (minims blurred; "festina tunc te"?)
image-009 L6   [d]elicias ⁊ hono
image-009 L7   [.]pectando ut d^a^(?)    (small letter above the final d)
image-009 L8   [.]sent^ri^(?). t̄n bn̄ ꝑci (tamen bene perci..?; "ri" above)
image-009 L9   [.]ō ē tutū q̄(?) abd      (non est tutum .. abd..?)
image-009 L10  [.]ione [rest smeared and stained - illegible]
image-009 L11  [tops of letters only at the cut edge]

RIGHT COLUMN (first 4-6 letters of each line only)

image-008 L1   ꝯg̃gan[
image-008 L2   dian(?)[
image-008 L3   tiōs e(?)[
image-008 L4   dauit[
image-008 L5   ⁊ ꝯg̃ga[                  (small "e" above)
image-008 L6   eris ī l(?)[
image-009 L1   = image-008 L5 (overlap)
image-009 L2   = image-008 L6 (overlap)
image-009 L3   inc̃(?) ei[               (small mark above)
image-009 L4   ꝓ me.[                   (red touch at the edge after it)
image-009 L5   gregā[
image-009 L6   ibi. il(?)[
image-009 L7   fra(?)[
image-009 L8   [trace of one letter at the diagonal cut]

======================================================================
PIECE B, SIDE SHOWN IN image-004 (tiles image-005 upper, image-006 lower)
======================================================================
Margin (left of column): paraph-like sign beside L2-L3; blue pen flourishes at
L1 level and at L7 level; red-and-blue descender bar beside L9-L11. No marginal
words.

SINGLE COLUMN (line-beginnings; right part cut away; surface abraded with white
loss in L1-L5, and a hole in L6-L7)

image-005 L1   ute[..]ant'(?) u[        (middle letters abraded; ends in -ant with
                                        a superscript "ur"-type sign)
image-005 L2   p̄a(?) mons(?) m[         (abraded; "mons" or "mous")
image-005 L3   ꝓp̄ [.]ortuū(?) su[       (propter .. ; second word abraded)
image-005 L4   ei d[.](?) q^i^ pc̄ce(?)[  (abraded; small letter above q)
image-005 L5   up[...]. ȝ h'[           (middle illegible - abrasion)
image-006 L1   = image-005 L4 (overlap)
image-006 L2   = image-005 L5 (overlap)
image-006 L3   ē enī t[hole]s[.][
image-006 L4   tes cla[hole]sus(?)[     ("clausus" possible but the middle is the hole)
image-006 L5   mons(?) n̄ hēd(?)[        (same doubtful word as image-005 L2)
image-006 L6   de ip̄o uō ty(?)[         (de ipso uero ..?)
image-006 L7   car[..]ta(?) ee(?) co[   (run of blurred minims; perhaps "esse")
image-006 L8   ut ī dn̄a(?) cl[          (overline over the first words)
image-006 L9   [.]p̄m de celo[
image-006 L10  [..]ipit(?) cē l[        (first letters lost at the diagonal cut)

======================================================================
PIECE B, OTHER SIDE, image-010 (tiles image-011 upper, image-012 lower)
======================================================================
Margin (right of column): blank apart from a faint show-through of the paraph
sign beside L2-L3 and a brown stain. Thin diagonal pen-strokes after several
line-ends look like line-fillers or hair-strokes, not letters.

SINGLE COLUMN (line-ends; left part cut away; hole in L6-L7)

image-011 L1   [.]ph'i(?) mal' ad
image-011 L2   [.]t ut ip̄m cō
image-011 L3   [.]cipit'(?) ei q̃^n^ co     (small "n"/"u" above)
image-011 L4   [.]uuat(?) ꝯstiit(?).      (a 9-shaped sign before "stiit"; uncertain)
image-011 L5   [.]i ꝯ^t^ reclamā          (9-shaped sign with "t" above)
image-011 L6   ⁊ n[hole]im(?) q̃to(?).
image-012 L1   = image-011 L5 (overlap)
image-012 L2   = image-011 L6 (overlap)
image-012 L3   [.]te[hole]es(?) sc̄(?) cā(?)
image-012 L4   [.]andam(?) d^i^ co'(?)     (blurred; small letter above d)
image-012 L5   [.]. i. filios eiu
image-012 L6   [.]atu(?). J(?)oe(?)^v^     (a red-touched capital, J/I-like, then
                                          two or three letters with a small sign
                                          above; possibly a short citation
                                          siglum - not resolved)
image-012 L7   [.]edat(?) q̃nto ei          ("cedat"/"ledat" ..; quanto?)
image-012 L8   [.]ito. es(?) ⁊ ꝓ(?)
image-012 L9   [.]ito ui(?)[               (cut by the diagonal edge)

SELECTED / UNREAD
- Selected: everything; the fragments are so small that I listed every visible
  line rather than choosing spans. Nothing was left unread by choice.
- Best anchors for a later source match (each still a part-line):
  image-002/003 right column: "sicut vestis ... / ..tis sine pelle n.. / et
  panno non suffi.." and, after the blue initial, "[C]ongrega.. / solent te.. /
  congregati ut ..".
  image-008/009 left column: "..congrega.. / .. quanto plures(?) / .. sed
  uellera ouium / .. tanto melius est / .. tempore quo congregato / .. in
  omnibus populis / nos la..abunt / festina.. / [d]elicias et hono.. /
  ..pectando ut .. / .. tamen bene perci.. / non est tutum ..".
  These expansions are my proposals; the abbreviated forms above are what is
  on the parchment.

LIMITATIONS
- No full line anywhere: piece A lacks the left of one column and the right of
  the other on each side; piece B has one column edge per side.
- Which side of each piece is recto, and the order of the two columns across
  the turn, cannot be told from these images. On piece A the side with the blue
  initial (image-001) and the side beginning "..congrega.." (image-007) clearly
  share the "congreg-" vocabulary, but I cannot fix their sequence.
- Tiles are low resolution; minims (u/n/m/i) and c/t are often indistinguishable,
  and several readings marked (?) are guesses at letter-shapes, not at sense.
- Piece B image-005 is abraded in L1-L5; holes interrupt image-006 L3-L4 and
  image-011 L6 / image-012 L3.
- A wider view is not available here; an adjacent strip of the same columns, or
  a higher-resolution capture of these four faces, would be needed for any
  connected prose.
